observed_vs_expected: Expected: (1) best_target_score should rise as cavity thickness approaches λ/2; actual score rose from 0.8689 to 0.9757, then sharply collapsed to 0.7682 in round 5. (2) tightest_margin should remain stable if symmetric design is viable; actual margin is 0.5656, remaining stable and robust. (3) if hypothesis fails, best_target_score will plateau below 0.95 or tightest_margin will degrade; actual behavior exhibits the score-collapse branch but does so abruptly rather than gradually plateauing.
deviation_mechanism: The performance collapse is driven by destructive optical path length (OPL) drift in the central spacer region. Between the third and fourth recorded thickness vectors, layer 8 increased by +15.3 nm and layer 10 increased by +15.6 nm, while layer 9 decreased by -30.0 nm. This aggressively displaces the central cavity optical thickness away from the quarter-wave resonance condition required for maximum reflectivity. Because the tightest margin remains high (0.5656), the geometry is not clashing or violating fabrication limits; instead, the refractive-index contrast is being misapplied spectrally, causing transmission spikes inside the target stopband.
continue_rationale: Five rounds have been executed with a historical peak of 0.9757. The drop to 0.7682 represents an optimizer overshoot that crossed a stability threshold, not a hard physical infeasibility. The tightest margin remains at 0.5656, confirming the design space is unconstrained and recoverable. Restricting the volatile spacer layers will likely restore performance within the existing physical hypothesis.
insight_for_next: Re-initialize layers 7 through 11 to their round-1 baseline values and apply a strict ±10 nm box constraint during the next optimization pass. Alternatively, fix layers 8 and 10 to nominal λ/4 optical thickness targets derived from the measured refractive indices, freeing only layers 7 and 9 for gradient descent to stabilize the cavity resonance before allowing broader refinement.
insight_grounding: The collapse is directly attributable to measurable parameter drift: layer 8 thickness jumped from 196.0068113274118 nm (vector 3) to 211.289526679253 nm (vector 4); layer 10 jumped from 202.81137026036112 nm to 218.43796294923243 nm over the same interval. This coincides precisely with the score falling from 0.9476638580210054 to 0.7682218012942811, while the tightest margin stayed constant at 0.565617885123679, isolating the cause to resonant detuning rather than constraint violation.
